summary: Selected the cross-review-surviving mutated finite adverse-transducer/COPY audit and attacked its first explicit realization. Exact search found a diagonal signed splice: the N=8 false-111 NAND selector (0,1,2,2,2,2,2,-1), of energy 56, can occur on both sides of a legal 11 COPY fiber. Exhaustion of all 378 saturated binary-signature COPY multisets of ranks 2 through 8 and both port orientations gives zero affine-span/boundary/glue residual and total anchor energy 112+N, between 114 and 120. Thus plain affine gluing has no strict transfer mechanism; this is finite evidence only and does not refute an augmented quaternionic coupling.
hypothesis: Causal mechanism: a complete P-adic transducer should force every repeated adverse state through COPY to gain valuation. Expected frontier move: exclude grade-zero/zero-gain NAND-COPY-NAND transitions and eventually certify sufficient P-adic gain. Falsification condition: a reachable signed adverse selector passes through a legal COPY state without any emitted transfer residual. The explicit affine-only realization meets that falsification condition via the false111-COPY11-false111 splice.

tests.finding: Enumerated 378 saturated COPY codes through rank 8 in both orientations; every code admits the exact zero-residual diagonal splice with energy in [114,120].

next_experiment: Require any proposed quaternionic NAND-COPY coupling to emit an explicit transfer coordinate that is nonzero on the repeated false-111 selector. For each candidate, enumerate all P^3 lifts of its normalized P^2 class, including DROP and internal zero-boundary kernels, and return either a carry/lumpability counterexample or an exact positive-gain certificate; do not infer all-depth transfer from a finite pass.
